newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police block activists at Japanese consulate.
newsitem.headline: HK police block activists at Japanese consulate.

text.p: A group of Hong Kong activists, who planned to travel to Tokyo to protest Japan's control over disputed islands in the East China Sea, were blocked from entering the Japanese consulate to apply for visas on Wednesday.

About a dozen policemen formed a human wall to block three activists from the Action Committee for Protection of the Diaoyu islands when they tried to enter the consulate in a building in Hong Kong's Central district to apply for visas.
The three men, two of whom are legislators, refused to allow the policemen to take their applications into the consulate and tore up the forms after leaving the building.

"It's incomprehensible for the police to do something like that. If the Japanese consulate were to shut the door in our faces, let them do it, it's none of their (police) business," said legislator Albert Ho.
Fury over the islands, known as the Diaoyu in China and Senkaku in Japan, was whipped up again last week after a Japanese group, led by a legislator, landed on one of them.

The cluster of islands, which are separately claimed by China, Taiwan and Japan, were the source of fiery nationalist passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan last year after a Japanese rightwing group built a lighthouse on one.

The Hong Kong activists decided to fly to Tokyo and stage a protest after a shortage of funding and pressure from the Taiwanese government forced them on Tuesday to indefinitely postpone a planned voyage to the islands.
